content.text: IV Drip Flow Rate Estimator
IV Drip Flow Rate Estimator: an offline mobile computer-vision application that estimates IV drip flow rates from a phone camera for nursing teams.
Executive Summary

A medical technology provider (unnamed) worked with HumbleBeeAI on a mobile application intended to help healthcare professionals estimate IV drip flow rates. Manual drop counting takes staff attention and may vary with distraction, fatigue, lighting and observer skill. The case-study describes an iOS/Android camera-based estimator that operates without internet access. Its reported measurements are source claims, not independently validated; deployment and production status have not been provided.

Context and Challenge

Traditionally, nursing staff count drops manually while monitoring IV delivery. The source says this requires continuous attention and can produce inconsistent readings, particularly amid distraction or fatigue; visibility, lighting and differences in observer skill are also cited as sources of variation. Staff may spend up to 3 minutes per observation, according to the case-study. The source does not provide a matched comparison protocol or clarify the settings in which those conditions were assessed.

attrs.chunkText: Accurate IV flow rate monitoring is essential in hospitals to ensure that patients receive the correct dosage of fluids or medication. Traditionally, nurses have relied on manual counting of drops, which requires continuous attention and can lead to inconsistency, especially in high-pressure environments. Recognizing this challenge, the client aimed to create a smart, mobile-based solution that could automatically determine IV flow rates using the device's camera. The objective was to deliver fast, precise, and real-time measurements while maintaining full patient privacy and reliability in any healthcare environment.

Traditional IV monitoring methods, while simple, present several operational and clinical limitations:

Human Error: Counting drops manually often results in inconsistent readings due to distractions or fatigue.

Time-Intensive: Staff must dedicate up to 3 minutes per observation, which is unsustainable when managing multiple patients.

Delayed Detection: Problems like air bubbles, occlusions, or incorrect drip speeds may go unnoticed for several minutes.

Inconsistent Accuracy: Variations in lighting, visibility, and observer skill levels lead to unreliable data.

In a busy hospital setting, these limitations reduce efficiency, increase cognitive load on nurses, and can affect patient care outcomes.

content.text: Solution and Capabilities
Camera-based flow-rate estimation

The delivered capability described is an application for iOS and Android that uses a device camera to estimate IV flow rate. A healthcare professional points the phone at the IV setup; the app displays an estimate within seconds. The source describes the operation as real time and offline, supporting use where internet access is unavailable.

content.text: Designed to reduce manual counting

By automating the drop-counting step, the application is intended to reduce the time and attention required for a manual observation and provide a consistent estimate. The case-study describes support for on-site healthcare staff, including in hospitals, clinics and remote facilities; actual production availability in those environments is not specified.
Results and Business Impact

The case-study reports over 95% accuracy for the camera-based, offline iOS/Android application and results within 15 seconds, compared with manual observations taking up to 3 minutes. It also characterizes the speed difference as over 10x faster than manual counting. These are reported measurements, not independently validated results. The source gives no accuracy tolerance, reference instrument, validation sample, lighting or device test matrix, or matched-pair basis for the speed comparison. The supplied record does not establish measured clinical outcomes or patient benefit; no business-impact measurement has been provided.
